title: Regional fallback topology for regulated retail POC
content:
Purpose
This note captures a latency-first hybrid deployment topology for the upcoming regulated retail POC (EMEA retail chain). Goal: keep median inference p95 <= 180ms for search/completion flows while meeting local data residency and audit constraints.

Context and constraints
- Retail POC scope: product search autocomplete + personalized snippet generation + in-store kiosk chat. Peak qps estimate: 300 qps across region during promotions; baseline 40 qps.
- Data sovereignty: customer requires that PII and audit logs remain in EU region (must not leave FR/DE data centers). Model artifacts may be pulled from hosted catalog but audit trail must be retained in-customer region.
- Budget guidance: POC cost target ~ $12k/month (infrastructure + Redwood reserved capacity credit).
- Latency SLO: p50<80ms p95<180ms for user-visible interactions. Offline batch jobs (embeddings, indexing) not latency sensitive.

Proposed topology (high level)
1) Primary runtime: Redwood Dedicated pools in EU-west zone (dedicated capacity for predictable throughput). Dedicated pool handles the majority of live traffic (can be autoscaled inside commitment).
2) Regional cache/edge: Lightweight prefix KV cache + small LLM shard hosted on private tenancy (customer VPC, private deployment) colocated with retail data to serve extremely low-latency kiosk reads and to keep sensitive context local. Kiosks route to this local private node for requests where context includes local inventory/PII.
3) Cross-region fallback: A hosted Redwood API tier (hosted) in nearby region configured as fallthrough for overload/capacity gaps or during DR. Sensitive payloads are stripped before routing to hosted fallback.
4) Smart router: Policy-based routing in front (Redwood routing policies) that considers request attributes: sensitivity flag, route by latency budget, prefer local private node -> dedicated pool -> hosted fallback.

Behavioral flow (examples)
- Kiosk request with local inventory context (marked sensitive): route to local private node; if local node unavailable, degrade to dedicated in same EU region with a strict audit that data was forwarded (and log entry created). No direct routing to hosted fallback for sensitive requests.
- Mobile app autocomplete (non-PII): route to dedicated pool; if p95 latency exceeds 180ms due to load, route subset of requests to hosted fallback (non-sensitive) with A/B observability flags.

Operational controls and safety
- Data tagging: clients must set sensitivity header. Router enforces policy.
- Audit log flow: All routed requests write immutable audit records to customer-managed S3 in EU and to Redwood control plane logs for operational debugging (control plane logs redacted to remove PII).
- Canary & rollouts: Start with 80% traffic to dedicated, 20% to private node for kiosks; ramp rules and automatic rollback if quality/latency regressions detected (use Redwood Console trace hooks).
- Rate limiting and quotas per route to prevent noisy-tenant effects.

Capacity & cost sketch (rough)
- Dedicated pool: baseline 4 GPUs (A10G-equivalent) to hit 300 qps with batching tuned for short sequences — estimated infra ~$9k/mo with reserved commit (pooled).
- Private node (kiosk): 1 small GPU (or CPU-quantized variant) colocated on customer edge box — estimated infra + install $1.5k/mo amortized.
- Hosted fallback usage (cold): expected <5% traffic, variable cost; budget $1.5k/mo.
- Total POC monthly ~ $12k/mo (matches target) — conservative, will refine after small load test.

Tradeoffs (explicit)
- Latency vs cost: Dedicated + private gives best p95 but increases ops complexity. A pure-hosted approach would be much simpler but risks data-residency non-compliance and possibly slightly higher median latency under heavy load.
- Operational surface: Adding private nodes increases deployment and update burden (patching, HSM if required). We recommend automation playbook before POC sign-off.
- Failure modes: If private node fails, sensitive flows must not leak to hosted fallback — revert to dedicated within region at cost of slightly higher latency.

Implementation checklist (POC milestones)
- Week 0: finalize sensitivity header schema and router policy definitions (SE-4821).
- Week 1: provision dedicated pool (4 GPUs) and baseline perf tests with representative prompts.
- Week 2: deploy private kiosk node in customer VPC + KV cache; end-to-end test for kiosk flows.
- Week 3: configure hosted fallback and set routing rules; run chaos tests (force dedicated pool throttling) to validate fallback behavior.
- Week 4: run customer-facing demo, collect telemetry, adjust thresholds and cost tuning.

Open questions / risks
- Can the customer accept the partial forwarding of redacted context to hosted fallback for non-sensitive flows? (Need legal sign-off.)
- What exact SLA for private node maintenance does customer require? On-call/patch windows will impact staffing and cost.
- Quantization tradeoffs: kiosk private node may need int8 quantized model; validate quality delta for snippet generation.
- Backup plan if dedicated pool provisioning takes longer than 2 weeks — temporary heavier reliance on hosted API.

Notes to self (informal)
- Get alignment with security on audit tail for cross-region logs — Priya to own.
- Add small diagram in Confluence showing policy decision tree (TODO).
- Obtain customer inventory API contract so we can estimate token size and prefix-cache hit rate.

Decision recommendation (short)
Proceed with hybrid: Primary Dedicated + local private node for sensitive kiosk flows + hosted fallback for non-sensitive overflow. This balances p95 latency goals and data residency constraints while keeping the POC within the cost target.

Next steps
- Review this doc with product/security + customer on Thurs 11/6 meeting.
- Spin up smoke cluster and gather first week telemetry; iterate on batching and cache TTLs.

Attachments / references
- See linked artifacts for tickets and draft config PR.

-- end of note --
